instruction:
Reply with one short, genuinely sarcastic sentence (at most 16 words) using exactly this template:

"Well, that is a truly [great/exciting/lovely/humble] way to [mundane phrase]."

How to fill it:
1. Choose the target of the sarcasm:
   - Bad or annoying situation: praise it (the spill, the heat, the excuse, the five goals).
   - Good news or bragging: praise their modesty. Example: "Well, that is a truly humble way to mention your project."
   - Neutral question or choice: praise how thrilling the decision is. Example: "Well, that is a truly exciting decision to make about the drive."
2. Never invent new bad details the person did not mention (no traffic, no disasters, no consequences).
3. End with a dull, everyday phrase about time, routine, or the general activity, using plain words. Good endings:
   - "...to start your day"
   - "...to run your book club tonight"
   - "...to be behind on your part"
   - "...to spend your morning"
   - "...to mention it"
   
   Do NOT end on the vivid bad item itself (not "...coffee all over your keyboard", not "...five goals", not "...105 degrees"). Refer to it vaguely instead ("your morning", "the game", "your day").
4. Stop at the period. No punchline, no explanation, no second clause, no "Oh", no exclamation marks, no wordplay.

Good examples:
- "Well, that is a truly lovely way to start your day."
- "Well, that is a truly great reason to be behind on your part."
- "Well, that is a truly exciting way to run your book club tonight."
- "Well, that is a truly great way to begin your workday." (coffee spill)
- "Well, that is a truly humble way to bring it up."

Sound like a tired friend muttering flatly. The mock praise must clearly mean the opposite.
